evidence: paper: A_n = \mathcal{A}_n, \qquad B_n = u_{\theta,n}e_\theta, \qquad p_n = q^{-2A+\lambda_n}\Pi_n, \qquad T_n = q^{-A-1/2+\lambda_n}\mathcal{T}_n.

provenance.note: machine audit: worker, gate, reviewer; not confirmed by a human

verdicts.summary: Lean has an equivalent formula. Three entries are Lean definition bodies with the paper's exponents: A_n is slot 0 of the bundle (the radial average of the axial coefficient) with q-exponent -A, i.e. H = S_n/s, in streamFactor; p_n is slot 2 with exponent -2A in basePressure; the stress pair T_n = (T_theta, T_z) is slots 3 and 4 with exponent -A-1/2 in baseStressTheta and baseStressAxial. The order factor q^{lambda_n} = q^{2hn} comes from positiveCoefficient/powerCoefficient inside slowSum (SlowBorelBase.lean:61, 245, 254). The fourth entry is packaged differently: Lean has no velocity-level entry B_n = u_{theta,n} e_theta; the swirl is the axial component K = swirlPotential of the same vector potential, with exponent 1/2 - A on -C^{-1} times the radial primitive of phi_n. The paper's entry is recovered by stated declarations: partialS_swirlPotential gives d_s K = -C^{-1} q^{-A-1/2} Sum chi q^{lambda_n} phi_n, and baseVelocity_angularMoment gives x_0 u_1 - x_1 u_0 = r^2 C^{-1} q^{-A-1/2} Sum chi q^{lambda_n} phi_n, which is r times the cut sum of the paper's u_{theta,n} = r q^{-A-1/2+lambda_n} phi_n / C from (5.1). The uncut finite version is also stated (prefixSwirl_radial, prefixVelocity_eq_profiles). velocity_zero/one/two show the K part of the curl is purely azimuthal. The Lean states this for the summed and prefix fields, not as a per-order tuple entry, and the slow base is not fed through the generic tuple lemma (GenericTupleRealization is referenced only inside the Generic* files). I did not check that the concrete Coefficients instances (FinalSlowBase.coefficients etc.) are the paper's Pi_n and T_n as functions; only the slots and exponents were matched.
